subjectEn: HomelabDeck, issue #2: a one-line installer, local AI guides and 7 new apps
subjectBg: HomelabDeck, issue #2: a one-line installer, local AI guides and 7 new apps
bodyEn:
HomelabDeck, issue #2

Since the first issue we published 7 new guides, grew the directory from 19 to 26 apps and released a free installer. Everything below was run in our own Proxmox homelab, and the numbers are the ones we measured.

New: the hldeck installer

hldeck is a free, MIT-licensed script that sets up a homelab stack with one command on a clean Debian or Ubuntu machine. The starter profile installs Homepage, Uptime Kuma, Portainer and Nginx Proxy Manager. The media profile installs Jellyfin, Seerr, Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr and qBittorrent behind a VPN kill switch, and there is a media-lite profile without the VPN. Image versions are pinned, and the script is short enough to read before you run it.

See the installer

Local AI on one GPU

  • Guide: a private ChatGPT-style assistant with Ollama and Open WebUI
    A 20B model on an RTX 3090 answered at over 120 tokens per second, with the honest limits of open models.
  • Guide: AI images at home with ComfyUI
    SDXL images in about 9 seconds, prompts and pictures stay on your own hardware.
  • Guide: share one NVIDIA GPU between Proxmox LXC containers
    Host driver, device nodes, the config lines and the reboot trap.
  • Guide: aider, OpenCode and Codex CLI on a local model
    Four tasks each: OpenCode passed 4 of 4, aider 3 of 4, Codex CLI 1 of 4. Plus the context-size trap.
  • Guide: Tuxee in a Proxmox LXC
    Browser terminals that keep running after you log out, in a process that used about 21 MB of RAM at start.

Media and passwords

  • Guide: Jellyfin, Sonarr and Radarr in one Proxmox LXC
    Compose file, folder layout, wiring and the mistakes to avoid.
  • Guide: migrate Vaultwarden from SQLite to PostgreSQL
    Tested with pgloader on Vaultwarden 1.37.5, with what our test did not cover.

The catalog

Seven apps joined the directory: Ollama, Open WebUI, ComfyUI, TTS-WebUI, Homepage, AdGuard Home and Tuxee. Each has real screenshots and a measured footprint. The week 46 note sums them up in one page.

Read the week 46 note
